terms.meaning: A short name made of lowercase words and dashes, used in a web address.
Marks a build to appear in the home page's Selected Work list, in the order given by its number.
Finding an item in a table by its key.

used_by: Home page and project pages (paths not visible in this packet)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the build list
sections.what: Brings in the list of builds and its type so this file can attach page details to each one.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page details are keyed by build id, so the build list is needed here.

sections.name: ProjectMeta
sections.title: Shape of the extra page details
sections.what: Describes the three extra fields a build can have for its page: a web name (slug), a short category, and an optional position in the home page's Selected Work list.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the field comments.
sections.watch_out: The category values are typed by hand, so they can drift from the build descriptions they are meant to follow.

sections.name: meta
sections.title: Page details for each build
sections.what: Lists each build's web name, category and featured position, keyed by the build's id. Featured positions 1 to 4 set the order of the Selected Work list on the home page.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping web names and home page order in one table lets them change without editing each build.
sections.watch_out: Two builds with the same featured number, or a gap in the sequence, would leave the home page order unclear.

sections.name: Project
sections.title: Project shape and combined project list
sections.what: Defines what one project entry looks like and builds the full project list by joining each build with its extra details. It also builds the featured list, which keeps only projects marked as featured and sorts them by their rank number.
sections.why: Keeps one combined record per project so other pages do not have to join the two sources themselves. Reason for the separate details source is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A project with no matching details entry gets no slug or category, and the displayed number depends on its position in the build list.

sections.name: getProject
sections.title: Find a project by its web name
sections.what: Returns the project whose slug matches the given text, or nothing if no project matches.
sections.why: Likely reason: project pages look up their own data from the web address.
sections.watch_out: It returns nothing when there is no match, so callers must handle a missing project.

sections.name: getProjectById
sections.title: Find a project by its internal id
sections.what: Returns the project whose internal id matches the given text, or nothing if none matches.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely used where places refer to projects by id instead of slug.
sections.watch_out: Ids and slugs are separate values, so a caller must use the one this function expects.

sections.name: relatedProjects
sections.title: Suggest projects with shared topics
sections.what: Suggests up to a set number of other projects that share at least one tag with the given project, ranked by how many tags they share. Tag matching ignores capital letters.
sections.why: Likely reason: to offer related projects at the bottom of a project page.
sections.watch_out: Projects sharing no tags are dropped, so a project with unusual tags may get no suggestions.

sections.name: splitSystemLabel
sections.title: Separate a leading label from a note
sections.what: Looks for a label wrapped in backticks at the very start of a research note and splits it from the rest of the text. If no such label exists, the whole text is returned unchanged.
sections.why: Likely reason: some notes start with a system name shown as a separate label. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The label must be wrapped in backticks and followed by a full stop, or it stays inside the text.

sections.name: ProcessStep
sections.title: Shape of a process step
sections.what: Describes one labelled step of a project's process write-up: a short label and the text under it.
sections.why: Gives every process step the same structure so the page can display them consistently.

sections.name: parseProcess
sections.title: Split a process write-up into steps
sections.what: Breaks a project's process description into paragraphs. A paragraph that starts with an all-capitals heading becomes a labelled step, a first paragraph ending in a colon becomes the intro, and everything else becomes a plain note.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the process section show clear steps without the writer marking them up.
sections.watch_out: Only headings written in capital letters become steps. A lowercase heading quietly turns into a plain note.

summary: Adds web-page details to each build, namely a short web name (slug), a category and an optional home page position. Only the first part of this file is visible in these notes.
purpose: Gives each build the details its own page and the home page need, which are not stored in builds.ts.
why: Likely reason: page details are kept apart from the build facts, and are keyed by build id.
how: First, the build list is imported. Then the extra fields are defined, and a table lists the details for each build id. Further functions in the file handle lookups and process steps, but their code is not visible in these notes.
inputs: Build ids from builds.ts and the hand-typed table.
outputs: The details table. The lookup helpers and the parsed process steps are outside these notes, so their outputs are not described here.
risks: Two builds with the same featured number would make the home page order unclear. Category text is typed by hand and can drift from the build description. Ids must match builds.ts exactly.
debug: If a build page has the wrong web address, check its slug in the details table. If the home page order is wrong, check the featured numbers. The lookup and process code, not visible here, is the place to look if pages fail to load.
